key_insight: AxiGSIS couples a kinetic solver with a macroscopic synthetic system to accelerate axisymmetric rarefied-gas and charged-particle simulations while preserving kinetic accuracy.
engineering_relevance: The method can reduce iteration counts and computational cost for near-continuum and moderate-Knudsen axisymmetric flows, making high-fidelity simulation more practical for nozzle, Couette, and electrostatic applications.
method: Finite-volume discrete velocity method on a 2D axisymmetric meridian plane with 3D molecular velocity space
Kinetic solver computes stress and heat flux, then passes them as source terms to a macroscopic synthetic system
Macroscopic updates feed back corrected primitive variables to the kinetic solver for rapid convergence
evidence_signal: The abstract reports validation on four benchmark problems—Taylor Couette, neutral nozzle expansion, charged-particle flow past an electrostatic sphere, and electrostatically accelerated charged-particle nozzle flow—showing agreement with reference kinetic solutions and fewer cells/iterations than conventional methods.
watch_item: Performance gains are emphasized for low and moderate Knudsen numbers, so convergence benefits may be less pronounced in highly rarefied regimes or if axisymmetric assumptions are violated.
paper_title: A general synthetic iterative solver for axisymmetric rarefied gas and electrostatic charged-particle flows
